---
title: "Recipes"
---

A shared cache does more jobs in a real app than caching. It elects a worker, counts requests, holds sessions and one-time tokens, remembers what was invalidated, and stands in for Redis wherever Redis was only ever there to hold a counter. Each recipe below starts with the moment you'd reach for one, then shows the pattern, then says where it stops working. The examples with output under them run against diskcache-oxide every time these docs are built, and the [example app](https://github.com/mikeckennedy/diskcache-oxide/tree/main/examples/webapp) puts most of these recipes together in one FastAPI app, tested.

## Caching

**[Caching expensive calls](caching-expensive-calls.qmd).** The cache-aside pattern, and `memoize`, which turns a function into a cached one keyed on its arguments.

**[Serving stale values while refreshing](stale-while-revalidate.qmd).** Keep a slow page or report available while one worker rebuilds it in the background, or refresh the hot keys ahead of time from a job, so readers never wait and the thundering herd is one worker.

**[Caching responses from other services](caching-http-responses.qmd).** Cache an upstream API's answers, honor its `max-age`, revalidate with ETags, and keep serving the last good answer when it's down.

**[Invalidating groups of keys](invalidating-groups.qmd).** Clear everything cached for one user, one product or one page at once: delete by key prefix, drop every entry with a tag using `evict(tag)`, or bump a generation number so stale entries are never read again.

**[Storing your own types](custom-types.qmd).** UUIDs, enums, timedeltas, Paths, dataclasses and Pydantic models in the cache with one registration each, and no pickle.

## Coordinating workers

For locks, semaphores and a throttle that hold across every process, see the [Coordination](../user-guide/coordination.qmd) guide page. The recipes here build on the same atomic calls.

**[Running a job once across workers](run-once.qmd).** Eight gunicorn workers each schedule the same hourly job, and you want it to run once. `add()` is atomic across processes, so exactly one of them claims it.

**[Rate limiting](rate-limiting.qmd).** Count requests per client in fixed time windows with `add()` and `incr()`, shared by every worker on the machine, with no Redis.

**[Counting things](counters.qmd).** View counts, download totals and usage quotas with `incr()` and `decr()`, flushed to the database with `pop()` so no count is lost or doubled.

**[Work queues](work-queues.qmd).** A queue every worker on the machine shares: `push()` at one end, `pull()` from the other, each item delivered to exactly one worker.

**[Single-use keys](single-use-keys.qmd).** Reset links, verification codes and idempotency keys: `pop()` hands a value to exactly one caller, and `add()` accepts a key exactly once.

## State

**[Server-side sessions](sessions.qmd).** Sessions every worker can read, with a sliding idle timeout from `touch()`, an absolute lifetime, and log-out-everywhere by key prefix.

## Deployment and testing

**[Sharing a cache across web workers](web-workers.qmd).** Where to put the cache directory, when to open it with gunicorn, uvicorn, FastAPI, Flask, Django and Celery, how to keep a busy cache from slowing requests, and what to do at shutdown.

**[Docker and Compose](docker.qmd).** One named volume for the caches and state, a fixed non-root user, the ownership rules that otherwise end in `PermissionError`, Kubernetes volumes, disk sizing, and the cleanup step after a format change.

**[Using the cache from asyncio](asyncio.qmd).** Read inline, write off the loop, and keep transactions on one thread, in FastAPI, Starlette or aiohttp.

**[Watching a cache in production](monitoring.qmd).** A health check and an admin endpoint: entries, bytes on disk, hit ratio across workers, the size limit, the write-ahead log, `check()` for damage, and the log lines worth alerting on.

**[Upgrading across a format change](upgrading.qmd).** When a release changes the on-disk format: the new release opens its own cache in a versioned subdirectory, old and new workers run side by side, `remove_old_formats()` cleans up afterwards, and what to do first about queues, counters and sessions.

**[Testing code that uses a cache](testing.qmd).** pytest fixtures for a real cache in a temporary directory, a `NullCache` for tests that shouldn't cache at all, and a fake clock for testing expiry without sleeping.

## In the user guide

Some features have more to them than a recipe can hold, so they have guide pages of their own: [Coordination](../user-guide/coordination.qmd) (locks, semaphores, `throttle`, `barrier`, `Averager` and `memoize_stampede`, which refreshes a hot value before it expires), [`FanoutCache`](../user-guide/fanoutcache.qmd) for many writing processes, and [Transactions](../user-guide/transactions.qmd). What's coming next is on the [roadmap](../user-guide/roadmap.qmd).
